text:
B: Alright! Can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hiya, you're a bit loud actually, but that's fine.
B: Ha, I get told that a lot. I'm Ryan, Stockport.
A: Aleena, Swansea. And before you say it, no, it's not Cardiff. Well, it's near Cardiff, but it's not Cardiff, yeah?
B: I wasn't going to say Cardiff! I was going to say I've been to Swansea once for a gig. Sin City, is it still going?
A: Oh my god, yeah, my friends go there all the time. That's so random.
B: Small world. Is this your first one of these calls?
A: Yeah, first one. Was your last one alright?
B: Yeah, he was sound. Man of few words, like. I reckon I did about ninety percent of the talking.
A: *(laughs)* I can believe that, ngl.
B: Cheeky! Go on then, what do you do?
A: First year at Swansea Uni, Business Management. And I work Saturdays in a sports shop in the Quadrant, and I flip trainers on Vinted on the side. I sold a pair of Air Forces last week for double what I paid. Double.
B: That's quality, that. That's proper business, that's better than the degree, honestly. I left uni after a year and I'm doing alright.
A: What do you do, then?
B: I run a bar and a music venue in the Northern Quarter, in Manchester. About eighteen staff, I do the booking, the bands, licensing, all of it. And I'm opening my own place in the next few years. Small bar, basement for gigs. I've got a mate with money, we're talking about it.
A: Wait, that's actually tidy. Do you get people on the guest list and that?
B: All the time. You'd be on it. You'd have to come up to Manchester, mind.
A: I'm moving to Manchester or London after uni anyway. That's where the money is. I want to go into sales or recruitment, somewhere with commission and a company car.
B: Nah, not recruitment. I've got mates in recruitment, mate, it's soul-destroying. Ringing people up all day who don't want to talk to you.
A: No, that's a bit of a stupid thing to say, you don't even know me. I'm brilliant at it. I'm the top seller on add-ons at work. I can get anyone to buy socks.
B: *(laughs)* Fair enough, fair enough, I'll give you that. Socks is hard. Nobody wants socks.
A: Nobody wants socks! But they buy them off me.
B: You should do the festival side. Ticketing, sponsorship, that sort of thing. You'd smash it, you've got the gob for it.
A: Thank you, I think? *(laughs)* Is that a compliment?
B: It's a compliment! What do you listen to, then? Go on, judge yourself.
A: UK rap, Afrobeats, whatever's on TikTok. And Malayalam film songs when my mum's driving, but that's not my choice.
B: We do an Afrobeat night once a month, it's rammed, it's one of the best nights we do. Whose turntable do you reckon that is behind me?
A: Yours, obviously. Do you DJ, then?
B: At mates' parties, yeah. I'm decent, to be fair. Better than most of the lads they book.
A: Everyone says that, though.
B: Not everyone's right, though, are they? I am.
A: Okay, go on then, what's the last thing you—
